en.commentary:
The price on the sticker buys you about half of what you will actually spend. That single fact reorders this entire category, and it is why I built this ranking on finished installed cost. I put the Generac Guardian 26 kW at number one because it is the only air-cooled machine here that carries a 200-amp service, a five-ton condenser and a well pump at the same time, and because Generac holds over 68% of the US home standby market, which translates into a dealer who can actually get a truck to your house the week after a storm. Generac's September 2026 catalog lists the 26 kW with the whole-house switch around $8,219. Add $400 to $2,500 for a transfer switch when it is quoted separately, $500 to $1,500 for gas line work, $200 to $600 for permits and plan review, and $3,000 to $6,000 for licensed electrical labor. A finished 26 kW job lands between $11,000 and $16,000, and the regional quotes I collected for a 24 kW install ran from about $8,500 in the Portland metro up past $22,000 in parts of the Northeast. Any list that ranks these machines by unit price is comparing a number you will never pay.

The second number worth your attention is the natural gas rating. Every manufacturer publishes two outputs, and the catalog headline is always the propane figure. The KOHLER 26RCAL is rated 26 kW on propane and 24 kW on natural gas. The Generac 24 kW drops to 21 kW on natural gas. The KOHLER 20RCAL drops to 18 kW. If your house is on a gas main, the smaller number is the one your air conditioner has to start against, and that gap of two to three kilowatts is exactly the margin that decides whether you buy the 22 kW or the 26 kW.

Third, your gas meter has a vote. A 24 kW Guardian pulls roughly 289 cubic feet per hour at half load, and a 22 kW unit wants about 220 cubic feet per hour at 5 to 7 inches of water column. Existing residential meters are frequently sized below that, and a meter upgrade runs $500 to $1,500 plus $150 to $500 in utility coordination fees, with two to four weeks added to the schedule because the utility controls the calendar. I have seen this single item turn a confirmed install date into a month of waiting.

On demand, the case for owning one of these is stronger in 2026 than it has been in a decade. EIA's Electric Power Annual put average US customer interruptions at 11 hours in 2024, close to double the prior decade's annual average, with Beryl, Helene and Milton accounting for 80% of it. NERC's January 2026 Long-Term Reliability Assessment placed 13 of 23 assessment areas at elevated or high resource adequacy risk and raised its summer peak demand forecast by 224 GW, most of it AI data center load. Grid Strategies has argued publicly that NERC's demand growth assumptions run high, and I think readers deserve both positions on the record. Either way, the direction of travel points at more hours in the dark.

One piece of housekeeping, because the error is circulating in market research reports: KOHLER home generators are sold by Rehlko, the name Kohler Energy took in September 2024 after Platinum Equity acquired majority ownership with Kohler Company retaining an investment stake. Briggs & Stratton has been owned by KPS Capital Partners since a September 2020 Section 363 asset sale. The two companies are independent of each other, and any report describing Briggs & Stratton as part of Rehlko is wrong.

highlights.title: Rank by the installed number, and read the sticker as a deposit
highlights.body: Seven line items decide what you pay: the generator, the automatic transfer switch at $400 to $2,500, the concrete or composite pad, gas line work at $500 to $1,500, a service panel upgrade when the existing one is full, permits and plan review at $200 to $600, and licensed electrical labor at $3,000 to $6,000. Labor alone routinely runs half the cost of the machine. A 22 kW natural gas install finishes at $9,000 to $13,500 in 2026, a 26 kW whole-home system at $11,000 to $16,000, and a 14 kW essentials unit at $6,000 to $9,000. I rank on those totals because that is the number that reaches your account.

highlights.title: The natural gas rating is the honest one, and it is always the smaller number
highlights.body: Manufacturers publish output for both fuels and marketing leads with propane. KOHLER's 26RCAL holds 24 kW on natural gas, the strongest gas-side figure in this field and the reason it sits at number two. Generac's 24 kW unit delivers 21 kW on gas, its 18 kW unit delivers 17 kW, and the KOHLER 20RCAL delivers 18 kW. If your home is on a gas main you should size against the gas column and treat the propane column as irrelevant. Getting this backwards is how people end up with a machine that drops the lights every time the compressor kicks in.

highlights.title: Your gas meter and your utility's calendar set the real install date
highlights.body: A 22 kW unit needs roughly 220 cubic feet per hour at 5 to 7 inches of water column, and a 24 kW Guardian draws about 289 cubic feet per hour at half load. Pipe sizing follows NFPA 54 from the meter to the pad, and long runs or undersized existing piping force an upsized line. When the meter itself is too small the utility has to swap it: $500 to $1,500 for the meter, $150 to $500 in coordination fees, and two to four weeks of waiting on their schedule. Ask your installer for the BTU demand figure and your meter's rated capacity before the deposit clears.

highlights.title: Champion's 14 kW aXis is the smartest money on this page for an ordinary house
highlights.body: It ships at $3,800 to $4,200 with a 200-amp whole-house transfer switch already in the box, carries a 10-year warranty against the 5-year standard from Generac, KOHLER and Cummins, and runs at 62 dBA, quieter than anything else here. The aXis controller communicates with the transfer switch over the home's existing wiring, which cuts installation labor and shows up as a smaller number on the quote. For a 1,800 to 2,500 square foot house with one air handler, a finished install at $6,000 to $9,000 does the same job a $14,000 system does.

highlights.title: Batteries win the first hour and fuel wins the third day
highlights.body: A Powerwall 3 at $15,300 to $16,200 transfers in milliseconds, makes no noise, burns nothing and needs no annual service, and at roughly $998 per kWh it prices about 13% under the EnergySage marketplace average. Its limit is 13.5 kWh of stored energy, so a multi-day outage depends entirely on solar recharging. A gas-fed standby unit runs as long as the main stays pressurized, which is the scenario that sells these machines in hurricane and ice storm country. Generac's PWRcell 2 at $17,000 to $21,000 for 9 kWh is the hedge, since it pairs with a standby generator and covers both patterns. Note that the federal Section 25D residential credit expired on 31 December 2025, so 2026 battery quotes carry no federal offset.

zh-tw.commentary:
先講結論，標價大概只買到你實際要花的一半。這一件事就足以把整個品類的排序重寫一遍，也是我這份榜單改用完工總支出排序的原因。

Generac Guardian 26kW 排第一，理由有兩個。第一是它是本榜唯一能同時撐住 200 安培總開關、五噸壓縮機跟抽水馬達的氣冷機種。第二是 Generac 在美國家用備用發電機市場的市佔超過 68%，講白了就是颱風過後你叫得到人，這件事在停電第三天的價值遠高於規格表上任何一欄。

Generac 2026 年 9 月的型錄把附全戶轉換開關的 26kW 機組標在 8,219 美元，換算約 NT$259,000。接下來要加的東西是：轉換開關若另外報價要 400 到 2,500 美元、燃氣管線 500 到 1,500 美元、許可與圖審 200 到 600 美元、持照電工人工 3,000 到 6,000 美元。26kW 完工落在 11,000 到 16,000 美元，也就是大約 NT$347,000 到 NT$504,000，差不多是台北一台國產中型房車的價格。我這輪蒐集到的 24kW 實際報價，波特蘭都會區約 8,500 美元，東北部某些地區超過 22,000 美元，同一台機器價差超過一萬三千美元。

第二個關鍵數字是天然氣出力。每家廠商都會公布兩個出力值，型錄大標永遠是液化石油氣那個比較好看的數字。KOHLER 26RCAL 是液化石油氣 26kW、天然氣 24kW；Generac 24kW 接天然氣掉到 21kW；KOHLER 20RCAL 掉到 18kW。你家如果接的是天然氣管線，冷氣啟動要對抗的就是比較小的那個數字，而這中間兩到三千瓦的差距，剛好就是你該買 22kW 還是 26kW 的分界線。

第三件事很多人買完才發現，瓦斯錶有投票權。24kW 的 Guardian 半載時每小時吃掉約 289 立方英尺天然氣，22kW 機種在 5 到 7 英寸水柱壓力下要 220 立方英尺。既有住宅瓦斯錶的容量常常不到這個數，換錶本身 500 到 1,500 美元，瓦斯公司協調費再 150 到 500 美元，工期還要往後加兩到四週，因為排程掌握在瓦斯公司手上。我看過這一項把已經敲定的安裝日整整往後推一個月。

需求面在 2026 年是十年來最強的。EIA 的統計顯示 2024 年美國用戶平均停電 11 小時，接近前十年平均的兩倍，其中 80% 來自 Beryl、Helene 與 Milton 三個颶風。NERC 2026 年 1 月的長期可靠度評估把 23 個評估區裡的 13 個列為風險升高或高風險，夏季尖峰需求預測一口氣上調 224 GW，主要來自 AI 資料中心。Grid Strategies 公開反駁，認為 NERC 的需求成長假設偏高，這一點我覺得讀者有權同時看到兩邊的說法。不過兩種立場指向同一個方向，就是停電時數會更多。

最後補一段台灣讀者的實話。這一整份榜單上的燒氣機種，台灣沒有家用代理，管線、電盤跟法規條件也對不上，價格欄位我一律標「約」表示是換算值。台灣這邊對應的其實是家用儲能跟大容量行動電源，20 kWh 是台灣家用儲能的隱形分水嶺，而且全國沒有住宅儲能的通案補助，補助都在地方而且多半綁著要一起裝太陽能。所以本榜第九到第十一名的三套電池方案，對台灣讀者的參考價值反而高於前八名。

highlights.title: 用完工價排序，標價當訂金看就好
highlights.body: 決定你實際掏多少錢的有七項：機組本身、自動轉換開關 400 到 2,500 美元、混凝土或複合底座、燃氣管線 500 到 1,500 美元、電盤容量不夠時的升級、許可與圖審 200 到 600 美元、持照電工人工 3,000 到 6,000 美元。光是人工這一項就經常等於機器價的一半。2026 年 22kW 接天然氣的完工價是 9,000 到 13,500 美元，26kW 全戶系統 11,000 到 16,000 美元，14kW 基本型 6,000 到 9,000 美元。我用這組總額排序，因為這才是真正從你帳戶扣走的數字。

highlights.body: 廠商兩種燃料的出力都會列，行銷文案永遠拿液化石油氣那個數字出來講。KOHLER 26RCAL 接天然氣還守得住 24kW，是本榜氣體側最強的，這也是它排第二的理由。Generac 24kW 機種接天然氣是 21kW，18kW 機種是 17kW，KOHLER 20RCAL 是 18kW。你家接天然氣就照天然氣那一欄挑機器，液化石油氣那一欄可以直接當作參考用。這件事搞反的下場很具體，就是壓縮機每次啟動全家燈都閃一下。

highlights.title: 真正的安裝日期由瓦斯錶跟瓦斯公司的行事曆決定
highlights.body: 22kW 機種在 5 到 7 英寸水柱壓力下每小時要 220 立方英尺，24kW Guardian 半載時約 289 立方英尺。從瓦斯錶拉到基座的管徑要照 NFPA 54 算，距離拉長或既有管線太細就得換粗的。瓦斯錶本身不夠力的時候只能請瓦斯公司換錶，錶 500 到 1,500 美元，協調費 150 到 500 美元，再等兩到四週。簽約付訂之前，直接跟安裝商要兩個數字：這台機器的 BTU 需求量，還有你家瓦斯錶的額定容量。

highlights.title: 一般住宅買 Champion 14kW aXis 最划算，這點我很有把握
highlights.body: 3,800 到 4,200 美元，換算約 NT$120,000 到 132,000，200 安培全戶轉換開關直接包在箱子裡，保固十年，Generac、KOHLER 跟 Cummins 都只給五年。運轉 62 分貝，本榜最安靜。aXis 控制器靠家裡既有電線跟轉換開關對話，電工時數少掉一截，這筆錢會直接反映在報價單上。50 到 70 坪、只有一組空調主機的房子，6,000 到 9,000 美元的完工價做的事情，跟 14,000 美元的系統是一樣的。

highlights.title: 電池贏在第一個小時，燃料贏在第三天
highlights.body: Powerwall 3 的 15,300 到 16,200 美元換來毫秒級切換、零噪音、不燒燃料、不用年度保養，每度容量約 998 美元，比 EnergySage 平台均價低約 13%。它的天花板是 13.5 kWh 的儲能量，停電超過一天就完全看太陽能補得回來多少。燒氣的備用機只要管線還有壓就一直跑，這正是颶風帶跟冰風暴帶的住戶願意掏錢的場景。Generac PWRcell 2 的 9 kWh 版本 17,000 到 21,000 美元算是兩邊都押的做法，它可以跟燃氣備用機併聯。另外提醒一件事，美國聯邦 Section 25D 住宅抵免已於 2025 年 12 月 31 日到期，2026 年的電池報價沒有聯邦補助可以扣。

en.commentary:
The ranking holds, and the calendar is the story this week. The Atlantic hurricane season peaks around the second week of September, which is when standby generator dealers take the most calls and can do the least about them.

The timing problem is simple arithmetic. A permit, a gas line, and a possible meter upgrade with two to four weeks of utility scheduling all stack up before the pad is poured and the unit is set. A generator ordered today protects you from late season storms at best, and it fully covers next year plus every winter ice storm in between. Generac's Guardian 26kW 7291 keeps the top spot on the strength of the best service network score in this list, 9.8, tied with the 24kW 7210, and that number matters more than nameplate output for most buyers because a standby generator you can't get serviced during a widespread outage is only half a solution. Kohler's 26RCAL stays a close second on the best natural gas output rating here, 9.5, for anyone whose house genuinely needs the full rated capacity after gas pressure derating.

Tesla's Powerwall 3 holds ninth again this week. Tesla confirmed this month that Powerwall 3 now works alongside existing Powerwall 2 units in mixed installations, a real expansion of the ecosystem for anyone who already owns one and wants to add capacity without replacing it. That's a genuine plus for existing Tesla households, but it doesn't move the Powerwall 3's rank here, because this list is scored primarily on multi-day outage runtime and gas supply independence, and a battery system without a generator backing it still runs out during an extended outage the way a natural gas or propane unit doesn't.

Champion's Axis 14kW continues to post the best installed-cost and permitting scores in this list, 9.7 and 8.4, making it the practical choice for buyers who want a straightforward install over maximum rated output. Generac's dealer density advantage is real, but it comes at a real price premium, and for a lot of households Champion's lower total cost of ownership is the smarter bet even sitting at third place here.

en.commentary: Generac's Guardian 26kW 7291 holds the top spot today, and the number that should drive most buying decisions in this category is service network. Raw output matters far less than most marketing suggests. Its 9.8 service network score, tied with the 24kW 7210, reflects something output ratings cannot capture: how fast a technician can actually reach your house when a transfer switch fails during a widespread outage, which is exactly the scenario a standby generator exists for. Kohler's 26RCAL holds second on a 9.5 natural gas output score, the strongest raw power delivery in this list, but its 8.4 service network score trails Generac by a full 1.4 points, a gap that matters more in a true regional outage than any kilowatt difference between the two. Champion's aXis 14kW holds third on the back of a 9.7 installed total cost score and a 9.6 outage runtime score, proof that a smaller, cheaper unit can still outlast bigger rivals on paper runtime when gas supply cooperates. Cummins' QuietConnect RS20AC earns its fifth place finish on a 9.0 noise score, the quietest unit in this entire ranking, worth real consideration for anyone installing next to a bedroom window or a neighbor's property line. With fall storm season approaching across much of the country, I would weight service network and installed cost over raw kilowatt output for most households, since an oversized generator sitting unrepaired during an outage protects nobody.
